facts.rationale: Clear a prose section label that is not a source identifier; this section contains two distinct canonical allocator objects.

facts.value: On a failed list allocation/insertion assertion, compiled code passes the source filename and applicable list/next/prev expression text to __assert. Under MUST_MATCH the explicit legacy line argument is used; otherwise the macro uses __LINE__. __assert reports the expression and calls HSD_Panic, which calls OSPanic after any returning panic callback. Successful checks bypass these diagnostics.
facts.rationale: Distinguish literal legacy line values from the actual pinned source lines and record the callback-return condition.

facts.value: Returns &dlist_alloc_data directly without allocation, mutation or an initialization check. HSD_ListInitAllocData configures that object for sizeof(HSD_DList) and alignment 4 when invoked; the getter itself does not establish that initialization already occurred.
facts.rationale: Remove the inherited unconditional initialized-descriptor guarantee.

facts.value: Allocates a node carrying the opaque data pointer and inserts it immediately after the supplied anchor. It returns the same anchor when non-NULL, or the new singleton when NULL. The anchor may be an interior node; this function does not locate the tail or a containing list head.
facts.rationale: The inherited purpose called an arbitrary anchor the list head; preserve the literal returned pointer.

facts.value: Asserts next is non-NULL. With non-NULL list, overwrites next->next with list->next, then sets list->next=next and returns list. With NULL list, overwrites next->next with NULL and returns next. It does not preserve a preexisting chain after next or check membership/aliasing; list==next creates a self-link.
facts.rationale: This is a single-node splice, not chain concatenation or validated insertion.

facts.value: Returns &slist_alloc_data directly without allocation, transformation or initialization check. HSD_ListInitAllocData configures the object when invoked. HSD_SListAlloc and HSD_SListRemove pass this descriptor to HSD_ObjAlloc and HSD_ObjFree.
facts.rationale: Do not infer that calling the getter forces or proves earlier initialization.

facts.value: NULL input returns NULL without allocator access. Otherwise saves list->next, passes only list to HSD_ObjFree and returns the saved pointer. It does not rewrite any predecessor or caller-owned head pointer, touch the saved successor, or free the opaque data payload. The caller must store the returned head or update any enclosing link.
facts.rationale: Distinguish the returned replacement pointer from an automatic mutation of the caller list.

facts.value: Startup calls this unit initializer, which resets and registers both allocator descriptors with alignment mask 3 and node-size strides. Allocation asserts success and zeros each SList node. Append inserts immediately after an anchor, overwriting the inserted node successor; prepend overwrites its node successor with the old head. Neither insertion validates aliasing. Removal frees only the supplied node and returns its saved successor, leaving caller head/predecessor updates and payload disposal to callers.
facts.rationale: State literal mutation boundaries and correct the ambiguous alignment-mask wording.

facts.value: Asserts prev is non-NULL, overwrites prev->next with list, and returns prev. No payload, allocator or old-head field is changed. Existing linkage after prev is discarded; prev==list produces a self-link because no alias check occurs.
facts.rationale: Record single-node insertion and aliasing boundaries visible in the entire body.

facts.value: HSD_ObjAllocData* HSD_DListGetAllocData(void). Takes no arguments and returns the persistent dlist_alloc_data descriptor address. HSD_ListInitAllocData configures this descriptor for HSD_DList nodes when invoked; the getter does not initialize it or check prior initialization.
facts.rationale: Do not imply that the getter guarantees descriptor configuration.

facts.value: Initialization passes separate SList and DList descriptors, node sizes and alignment 4 to the object allocator initializer. Singly linked construction allocates and zeros a node, stores the opaque payload and rewrites next links. Append returns the original non-NULL insertion anchor, which can be an interior node, or the new singleton for NULL. Prepend returns the newly inserted node. Remove returns the supplied node to its allocator and returns its saved successor; NULL removal returns NULL.
facts.rationale: Distinguish append anchor returns from replacement list heads.
